The petitioners vide the present petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure,
1973 seek quashing of FIR No.346/2018 dated 02.11.2018 registered under Sections 498A/406/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 at P.S Khyala, Delhi and all proceeding emanating therefrom in view of the Settlement dated 27.03.2023 arrived at between the parties.

2. This petition is accompanied by the Settlement dated 27.03.2023 [Annexure-P2] and is also supported by affidavits of all the petitioners and of respondent no.2, alongwith proofs of their respective I.Ds.
3. Petitioner nos. 1 to 5 and as also respondent no.2 are present in Court and have been identified by the IO.
Their credentials have been This is a digitally signed order.

4. Issue Notice.
5. Learned APP accepts notice.
He confirms that she has no objection to the quashing of the said FIR.

6. Respondent no.2 confirms that the petitioner no.1 and respondent no.2 have been granted divorce Sh. Rohit & Ors vs The State Nct Of Delhi, Delhi & Anr on 18 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/97761562/

sentences.text: She further affirms the Settlement dated 27.03.2023, whereby the petitioner no.1 has already paid her a sum of Rs.6,00,000/- the remaining amount of Rs.2,00,000/- has been handed over to the respondent no. 2 [vide DD no.383520 dated 08.08.2023 issued on Kotak Mahindra Bank] in full and final settlement of all her claims including alimony, maintenance (present, past and future), stridhan etc.
She states that she has no objection to the quashing of the present FIR.

7. In view of the settlement arrived at between the parties and following the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Jitendra Raghuvanshi & Ors. Vs. Babita Raguvanshi & Anr (2013) 4 SCC 58, Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab & Anr. (2012) 10 SCC 303 and Narinder Singh & Ors. vs. State of Punjab & Anr. (2014) 6 SCC 466, this Court is of the opinion that continuation of the aforesaid FIR will be an exercise in futility.
